subject.title: [Feature]: Option to force-prepend an opening <think> tag for local reasoning models

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class default-off synthetic `<think>` prepend contract in core config, or keep this behavior in provider/model-specific params and prompts?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this would add a long-lived config/default and output-format surface in an area where repository policy sets a high bar for new knobs and provider-owned behavior may be the better boundary.

options.title: Choose the owner boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open and do not dispatch automated repair until a maintainer decides whether the contract belongs in core config or provider metadata.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core option
options.body: Approve a default-off global/per-model setting with docs, schema, runner/subscriber wiring, native-tag guard, and streaming plus final-text proof.

options.title: Reject core config for now
options.body: Close or reframe the request around provider params/prompt templates if maintainers decide synthetic delimiter injection should not become an OpenClaw config contract.

recommendation.title: Choose the owner boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and do not dispatch automated repair until a maintainer decides whether the contract belongs in core config or provider metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the clearest current-history owner across the config, embedded subscriber, and adjacent reasoning-tag parser surfaces.
